diagnosis: The scenario failed the Weak Arm gate because all rollouts resulted in decisions that directly contradict the hidden information (PF1 and PF2) without any possibility of the model accessing them. Specifically, the models consistently chose 'worldwide' territories (contradicting C2/PF1), 'battery-management technology' (contradicting C4/PF2), '5%' royalty (contradicting C5/PF2), and 'sublicensing_allowed: true' (contradicting C6/PF2). While this shows the model is not 'leaking' the correct answers, it indicates the current prompt structure allows a lone agent to make a complete, coherent, but incorrect decision based solely on public facts S1-S4.

fix_instructions: To ensure the scenario requires multi-agent coordination, you must increase the tension between public facts and private facts. Currently, the model can easily default to 'standard' licensing terms (worldwide, 5%, sublicensing allowed) when public facts are ambiguous. Tighten checks C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, and C6 by ensuring the public facts (S1-S4) provide a strong, plausible, but incorrect baseline that specifically nudges the model toward the wrong decision unless PF1 and PF2 are integrated via conversation.
